rubrics.justification: Detailed description is broadly consistent with a 3AA blastocyst, including expansion, ICM, TE, and zona thinning, but it likely overstates image-resolvable details such as exact quadrant location, symmetry, and absence of subtle debris/vacuoles.
Thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor diagnosis, semen parameters, endometrium, first-cycle status, BMI, alcohol use, stress, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis.

Reasoning is structured and internally consistent, and the probability estimate generally follows from the case factors, though some quantitative adjustments (especially for alcohol/stress effects) are more assertive than firmly evidence-based.

Recommendations are largely consistent with IVF practice, especially support for single embryo transfer in a young patient with a high-quality blastocyst; minor deviations include overemphasis on PGT-A discussion and some speculative recommendations not standard after a first transfer.

Provides clear, practical next steps for this transfer and future planning, including SET, alcohol cessation, luteal support considerations, nutrition, follow-up, and contingency planning if unsuccessful.
